sections.heading: What is SME Banking?
sections.content:
SME Banking provides financial products, services and advisory support to micro, small and medium-sized enterprises. It serves registered companies, partnerships, household businesses and eligible entrepreneurs whose needs are more complex than personal banking but generally less specialized than large corporate banking.

A modern SME bank connects business identity, beneficial owners, accounts, payments, collections, liquidity, credit, trade, payroll, tax-related transactions, digital channels, relationship management and partner services. The objective is to help each enterprise run its daily operations reliably, manage cash-flow volatility, fund sustainable growth and control financial risk.

sections.heading: Who Does SME Banking Serve?

items.title: Start-ups and New Businesses
items.description: Newly established businesses requiring registration support, business accounts, digital banking, payment acceptance and an initial operating-finance foundation.

items.title: Micro and Household Businesses
items.description: Owner-managed businesses requiring simple collections, supplier payments, payroll, deposits, working capital and separation of personal and business finances.

items.title: Small Enterprises
items.description: Established small enterprises with regular turnover, employees, suppliers and recurring financing, cash-management and reporting needs.

items.title: Medium-Sized Enterprises
items.description: Growing businesses with more complex approval structures, multi-account operations, larger credit needs, trade flows and treasury requirements.

items.title: Merchants and Commerce Businesses
items.description: Retailers, distributors, restaurants and online sellers requiring QR, POS, payment gateway, reconciliation, inventory funding and settlement visibility.

items.title: Trading and Export Businesses
items.description: Importers and exporters requiring letters of credit, guarantees, documentary collection, supply-chain finance, FX and cross-border payments.

sections.heading: Core Product and Service Families

items.title: Business Accounts and Deposits
items.description: Business current accounts, multi-currency accounts, term deposits, virtual accounts, account hierarchies, mandates, entitlements and liquidity visibility.

items.title: Payments, Collections and Merchant Services
items.description: Domestic and international transfers, bulk payments, payroll, tax and bill payments, QR, POS, payment gateways, direct debit and automated reconciliation.

items.title: Cash and Liquidity Management
items.description: Cash-position dashboards, receivables and payables management, liquidity forecasting, sweeping, pooling, alerts and surplus-cash placement.

items.title: Business Lending and Working Capital
items.description: Overdrafts, revolving credit, working-capital loans, term loans, equipment finance, invoice finance, supply-chain finance and secured facilities.

items.title: Trade Finance and Foreign Exchange
items.description: Letters of credit, documentary collection, bank guarantees, import/export finance, FX conversion, hedging and cross-border settlement support.

items.title: Advisory and Business Services
items.description: Relationship management, business insights, sector expertise, insurance, employee banking, accounting integrations, API banking and partner services.

sections.heading: How the SME Banking Business Creates Value
sections.content:
SME Banking creates value through durable primary-bank relationships and a deep understanding of each customer's operating cycle. Revenue may come from lending margins, deposits, payments and collection fees, merchant acquiring, trade finance, foreign exchange, guarantees, cash-management services, insurance and partner propositions.

Sustainable growth depends on acquiring viable businesses, capturing operating accounts and transaction flows, retaining deposits, serving both borrowing and non-borrowing needs, pricing for risk, detecting early-warning signals and delivering efficient digital service. The bank should evaluate the enterprise, its owners, industry, suppliers, customers, cash-conversion cycle and repayment sources as one connected business context.

sections.heading: Business Needs and Relevant Solutions

items.title: Run Daily Financial Operations
items.description: Set up business accounts, digital banking, user roles, approval matrices, payment limits, payroll, tax payments and audit trails.

items.title: Collect Revenue Efficiently
items.description: Enable QR, POS, gateways, virtual accounts, receivables matching, direct debit and real-time collection notifications.

items.title: Manage Cash Flow and Liquidity
items.description: Use cash-flow dashboards, forecasting, sweeps, deposits, alerts and payables scheduling to maintain adequate liquidity.

items.title: Fund Working Capital
items.description: Match overdrafts, working-capital lines, invoice finance and supply-chain finance to inventory, receivables and seasonal cycles.

items.title: Finance Business Growth
items.description: Structure term loans, equipment finance, premises finance, guarantees and owner equity for expansion and capital investment.

items.title: Trade Across Borders
items.description: Support imports and exports through FX, international payments, documentary instruments, guarantees and trade-risk controls.

sections.heading: SME Sales Discovery Guide

items.title: Profile the Business
items.description: Understand legal form, ownership and beneficial owners, industry, operating history, locations, employees, products and business model.

items.title: Understand Operating Flows
items.description: Map major customers and suppliers, sales channels, monthly turnover, payment methods, currencies, seasonality and concentration risks.

items.title: Assess Financial Capacity
items.description: Review revenue, margins, expenses, assets, liabilities, bank statements, tax records, cash conversion and projected cash flow.

items.title: Define the Financing Need
items.description: Clarify the amount, purpose, timing, tenor, repayment source, collateral, guarantees and sensitivity to downside scenarios.

items.title: Design the Relationship Solution
items.description: Identify opportunities across accounts, collections, payments, payroll, liquidity, credit, trade, FX, insurance and integrations.

items.title: Confirm the Next Step
items.description: Agree documentation, KYC/KYB, credit assessment, approvals, pricing, covenants, activation, drawdown and ongoing review responsibilities.

sections.heading: Credit Assessment and Monitoring

items.title: Business and Ownership Verification
items.description: Validate incorporation, licenses, ownership, beneficial owners, authorized signatories, related parties and legal capacity to borrow.

items.title: Business Risk Assessment
items.description: Assess industry outlook, competitive position, customer and supplier concentration, seasonality and operational dependencies.

items.title: Financial Analysis
items.description: Analyze historical and projected revenue, profitability, leverage, debt-service capacity, working-capital cycle and cash-flow resilience.

items.title: Repayment and Security
items.description: Identify primary and secondary repayment sources and evaluate collateral ownership, valuation, enforceability, insurance and monitoring needs.

items.title: Credit Structuring
items.description: Set appropriate limits, tenor, pricing, conditions, covenants, approval authority and exception handling based on the risk profile.

items.title: Ongoing Monitoring
items.description: Monitor account behavior, arrears, covenant breaches, turnover decline, returned payments, sector stress and other early-warning indicators.

sections.heading: Responsible Banking and Risk Management
sections.content:
Every SME recommendation must be appropriate for the business purpose, financial capacity and risk profile. Teams must clearly explain pricing, interest, fees, collateral, guarantees, covenants, repayment obligations, FX and trade risks, default consequences, data use and complaint channels.

Customer due diligence must cover the legal entity, beneficial owners, controllers, authorized users and relevant related parties. KYB/KYC, AML, sanctions, anti-bribery, tax, fraud, credit, environmental and social risk, data privacy and product-governance controls must be completed through approved processes. SME Segment content supports product understanding and navigation; it does not replace approved product terms, credit policy, compliance guidance, legal advice or professional financial advice.

sections.heading: Ngân hàng SME là gì?
sections.content:
Ngân hàng SME cung cấp sản phẩm, dịch vụ tài chính và tư vấn cho doanh nghiệp siêu nhỏ, nhỏ và vừa. Phân khúc này bao gồm công ty, doanh nghiệp tư nhân, hợp tác kinh doanh, hộ kinh doanh và doanh nhân đủ điều kiện có nhu cầu phức tạp hơn khách hàng cá nhân nhưng thường chưa cần mô hình phục vụ chuyên biệt như doanh nghiệp lớn.

Ngân hàng SME hiện đại kết nối hồ sơ pháp lý doanh nghiệp, chủ sở hữu hưởng lợi, tài khoản, thanh toán, thu hộ, thanh khoản, tín dụng, thương mại, trả lương, giao dịch thuế, kênh số, quản lý quan hệ và dịch vụ đối tác. Mục tiêu là giúp doanh nghiệp vận hành ổn định, quản lý biến động dòng tiền, tài trợ tăng trưởng bền vững và kiểm soát rủi ro tài chính.

Nguồn thu có thể đến từ biên lợi nhuận tín dụng, tiền gửi, phí thanh toán và thu hộ, chấp nhận thanh toán, tài trợ thương mại, ngoại hối, bảo lãnh, quản lý dòng tiền, bảo hiểm và sản phẩm đối tác.

Tăng trưởng bền vững phụ thuộc vào việc thu hút doanh nghiệp có chất lượng, nắm giữ tài khoản vận hành và luồng giao dịch, duy trì tiền gửi, phục vụ cả nhu cầu tín dụng và phi tín dụng, định giá theo rủi ro, nhận diện cảnh báo sớm và cung cấp dịch vụ số hiệu quả. sections.heading: What is Enterprise Banking?
sections.content:
Enterprise Banking serves large companies, corporate groups and multinational organizations with complex financial structures, high transaction volumes and operations across multiple entities, currencies or markets. These customers usually require more than individual products: they need coordinated solutions covering treasury, payments, liquidity, working capital, trade, financing, risk management and digital integration.

A strong enterprise bank combines relationship management, sector expertise, credit structuring, transaction banking and specialist product teams. The objective is to provide visibility and control across the corporate ecosystem while helping the customer fund operations, invest in growth, manage market risk and execute strategic transactions efficiently.

sections.heading: Who Does Enterprise Banking Serve?

items.title: Large Domestic Corporations
items.description: Established enterprises with significant revenue, complex supply chains, high payment volumes and material working-capital or investment requirements.

items.title: Corporate Groups and Holdings
items.description: Parent companies and subsidiaries requiring consolidated liquidity, intercompany controls, centralized treasury and group-wide financing structures.

items.title: Multinational Companies
items.description: Organizations operating across countries and currencies that need cross-border payments, global cash visibility, FX management and coordinated banking coverage.

items.title: Infrastructure and Project Companies
items.description: Businesses delivering large projects that require long-tenor funding, guarantees, escrow arrangements, milestone payments and risk allocation.

items.title: Major Importers and Exporters
items.description: Companies with large trade flows requiring letters of credit, documentary instruments, supply-chain finance, guarantees, FX and sanctions controls.

items.title: Institutional and Public-Sector Entities
items.description: Eligible institutions requiring controlled collections, disbursements, liquidity management, reporting, financing and secure digital connectivity.

sections.heading: Core Product and Service Families

items.title: Corporate Accounts and Cash Management
items.description: Multi-entity and multi-currency accounts, virtual accounts, receivables, payables, pooling, sweeping, forecasting and consolidated cash visibility.

items.title: Payments and Collections
items.description: Bulk and real-time payments, payroll, tax, direct debit, merchant collections, host-to-host connectivity, APIs and automated reconciliation.

items.title: Trade and Supply-Chain Finance
items.description: Letters of credit, documentary collection, guarantees, import and export finance, receivables finance and supplier or distributor programs.

items.title: Working Capital and Corporate Lending
items.description: Overdrafts, revolving facilities, bilateral and syndicated loans, acquisition finance, asset finance and tailored working-capital structures.

items.title: Structured and Project Financing
items.description: Long-term and limited-recourse financing supported by project cash flows, contractual arrangements, security packages and financial covenants.

items.title: Markets and Risk Management
items.description: Foreign exchange, interest-rate and commodity risk solutions, deposits, investments, hedging and access to approved capital-markets capabilities.

sections.heading: How Enterprise Banking Creates Value
sections.content:
Enterprise Banking creates value through deep, long-term relationships and an integrated understanding of the customer's business model, industry, ownership, financial structure and strategic priorities. Revenue can come from credit margins, operating deposits, payments, cash management, trade finance, guarantees, foreign exchange, hedging, advisory and other approved specialist services.

The strongest relationships are anchored in daily operating flows rather than a single loan. Banks seek to become a primary or strategic banking partner by connecting treasury, transaction services, financing and risk management. Sustainable returns require disciplined capital allocation, risk-adjusted pricing, cross-product coordination, strong execution and continuous monitoring of both relationship value and credit exposure.

sections.heading: Enterprise Needs and Relevant Solutions

items.title: Gain Group-Wide Cash Visibility
items.description: Connect accounts across entities, banks and currencies through dashboards, reporting, host-to-host channels and approved API integrations.

items.title: Optimize Liquidity
items.description: Use pooling, sweeping, intercompany funding, forecasts, deposits and concentration structures to reduce idle cash and external borrowing.

items.title: Improve Transaction Control
items.description: Standardize payments, collections, approval matrices, limits, entitlements, reconciliation and audit trails across the organization.

items.title: Fund Operations and Growth
items.description: Match working-capital lines, term lending, syndicated facilities or structured finance to operating cycles and investment plans.

items.title: Support Trade and Supply Chains
items.description: Combine documentary trade, guarantees, receivables, supplier finance, distributor finance and cross-border settlement solutions.

items.title: Manage Financial Risk
items.description: Identify currency, interest-rate, commodity, liquidity and counterparty exposures and apply suitable approved risk-management solutions.

sections.heading: Enterprise Sales Discovery Guide

items.title: Understand the Corporate Structure
items.description: Map ownership, parent and subsidiary relationships, countries, legal entities, authorized signatories and treasury decision makers.

items.title: Map Operating Flows
items.description: Identify customers, suppliers, payment types, collection channels, currencies, transaction volumes, seasonality and cross-border corridors.

items.title: Review Treasury Operations
items.description: Understand cash visibility, liquidity concentration, forecasts, bank connectivity, approval controls, investments and funding practices.

items.title: Assess Financing Requirements
items.description: Clarify purpose, amount, tenor, repayment sources, security, covenants, project assumptions and required funding structure.

items.title: Identify Risks and Constraints
items.description: Explore industry, concentration, leverage, FX, interest-rate, commodity, country, compliance, technology and execution risks.

items.title: Build the Relationship Plan
items.description: Prioritize immediate needs, solution owners, stakeholder engagement, implementation steps, pricing, documentation and review milestones.

sections.heading: Credit Assessment and Ongoing Monitoring

items.title: Group and Ownership Analysis
items.description: Verify legal entities, beneficial owners, related parties, guarantees, intercompany dependencies and the strength of parental support.

items.title: Industry and Business Risk
items.description: Assess market position, strategy, competitive advantage, regulation, customer and supplier concentration and operating resilience.

items.title: Financial and Cash-Flow Analysis
items.description: Evaluate earnings quality, leverage, liquidity, debt-service capacity, cash conversion, forecasts and sensitivity to downside scenarios.

items.title: Facility and Security Structure
items.description: Align borrower, purpose, tenor, repayment, collateral, guarantees, covenants, conditions and documentation with identified risks.

items.title: Risk-Adjusted Relationship Return
items.description: Consider capital use, expected loss, operating deposits, transaction revenue, implementation cost and total relationship economics.

items.title: Early-Warning Monitoring
items.description: Track financial performance, account behavior, covenant compliance, ratings, market events, sector stress and management changes.

sections.heading: Responsible Banking, Governance and Controls
sections.content:
Enterprise solutions must be appropriate for the customer's stated purpose, authority, financial capacity and risk profile. Product teams must clearly explain pricing, interest, fees, collateral, guarantees, covenants, market risks, break costs, operational responsibilities and default consequences. Complex or structured solutions require the relevant specialist, credit, legal, compliance and product approvals.

Customer due diligence must cover the corporate group, legal entities, beneficial owners, controllers, authorized users and relevant connected parties. KYB/KYC, AML, sanctions, anti-bribery, tax, fraud, credit, country, environmental and social risk, data privacy and product-governance controls must follow approved processes. Enterprise Segment content supports business understanding and sales discovery; it does not replace approved product terms, credit policy, legal advice, compliance guidance or professional financial advice.

sections.heading: Ngân hàng Doanh nghiệp lớn là gì?
sections.content:
Ngân hàng Doanh nghiệp lớn phục vụ công ty quy mô lớn, tập đoàn và tổ chức đa quốc gia có cấu trúc tài chính phức tạp, khối lượng giao dịch cao và hoạt động trên nhiều pháp nhân, tiền tệ hoặc thị trường. Các khách hàng này thường không chỉ cần từng sản phẩm riêng lẻ mà cần giải pháp phối hợp về ngân quỹ, thanh toán, thanh khoản, vốn lưu động, thương mại, tài trợ, quản trị rủi ro và tích hợp số.

Một ngân hàng doanh nghiệp mạnh kết hợp quản lý quan hệ, chuyên môn ngành, cấu trúc tín dụng, ngân hàng giao dịch và các đội ngũ sản phẩm chuyên biệt. Mục tiêu là cung cấp khả năng quan sát và kiểm soát toàn hệ sinh thái doanh nghiệp, đồng thời hỗ trợ khách hàng tài trợ vận hành, đầu tư tăng trưởng, quản trị rủi ro thị trường và thực hiện giao dịch chiến lược hiệu quả.

sections.heading: Ngân hàng Doanh nghiệp lớn tạo ra giá trị như thế nào?
sections.content:
Ngân hàng Doanh nghiệp lớn tạo giá trị thông qua quan hệ sâu và dài hạn cùng sự hiểu biết tích hợp về mô hình kinh doanh, ngành, sở hữu, cấu trúc tài chính và ưu tiên chiến lược của khách hàng. Nguồn thu có thể đến từ biên tín dụng, tiền gửi vận hành, thanh toán, quản lý dòng tiền, tài trợ thương mại, bảo lãnh, ngoại hối, phòng ngừa rủi ro, tư vấn và các dịch vụ chuyên biệt được phê duyệt.

Quan hệ mạnh nhất được neo vào dòng tiền vận hành hằng ngày thay vì một khoản vay đơn lẻ. Ngân hàng hướng tới vai trò đối tác chính hoặc chiến lược bằng cách kết nối ngân quỹ, dịch vụ giao dịch, tài trợ và quản trị rủi ro. Hiệu quả bền vững đòi hỏi phân bổ vốn kỷ luật, định giá theo rủi ro, phối hợp liên sản phẩm, thực thi tốt và theo dõi liên tục giá trị quan hệ cùng mức độ rủi ro tín dụng.

sections.heading: Ngân hàng có trách nhiệm, Quản trị và Kiểm soát

Giải pháp doanh nghiệp phải phù hợp với mục đích, thẩm quyền, năng lực tài chính và hồ sơ rủi ro của khách hàng. Các đội ngũ cần giải thích rõ giá, lãi suất, phí, tài sản bảo đảm, bảo lãnh, covenant, rủi ro thị trường, chi phí tất toán, trách nhiệm vận hành và hậu quả vi phạm. Giải pháp phức tạp hoặc có cấu trúc cần phê duyệt phù hợp từ chuyên gia, tín dụng, pháp chế, tuân thủ và sản phẩm.

Thẩm định khách hàng phải bao phủ tập đoàn, pháp nhân, chủ sở hữu hưởng lợi, người kiểm soát, người dùng được ủy quyền và các bên liên quan. KYB/KYC, AML, cấm vận, chống hối lộ, thuế, gian lận, tín dụng, quốc gia, môi trường và xã hội, quyền riêng tư dữ liệu và quản trị sản phẩm phải tuân theo quy trình được phê duyệt. Nội dung phân khúc hỗ trợ hiểu nghiệp vụ và khám phá nhu cầu bán hàng; không thay thế điều khoản sản phẩm, chính sách tín dụng, tư vấn pháp lý, hướng dẫn tuân thủ hoặc tư vấn tài chính chuyên nghiệp.
